points.title: 贵族童年与早期教育
points.description: 维特根斯坦出生于维也纳一个极其富有的犹太裔工业家族，是家中八个孩子中最小的一个。他的父亲卡尔·维特根斯坦是钢铁业巨头，家族艺术氛围浓厚。路德维希接受了当时最好的教育，在家中被教导多种语言，包括英语、法语、德语。尽管家境优越，维特根斯坦却对家族财富感到不安，对自杀的念头萦绕心头。这段时期他展现出对工程和机械的兴趣，后来进入柏林工业大学学习机械工程，后又转向曼彻斯特航空工程研究，对数学基础产生浓厚兴趣。
points.descriptionEn: Wittgenstein was born in Vienna into one of Europe's wealthiest families, the youngest of eight children. His father Karl Wittgenstein was an industrial magnate in the steel industry. Despite immense wealth, Ludwig felt uneasy about his family's fortune and struggled with suicidal thoughts. He received an elite education, tutored at home in multiple languages. Initially drawn to engineering, he studied mechanical engineering in Berlin before moving to Manchester for aeronautical research, where he developed a profound interest in the foundations of mathematics.

points.title: 哲学启蒙与逻辑研究
points.description: 1911年，维特根斯坦前往剑桥大学，在伯特兰·罗素的指导下研究逻辑和哲学。罗素很快认识到维特根斯坦的非凡才能，称他为'天才中最纯粹的类型'。在剑桥期间，维特根斯坦深入研究了逻辑哲学问题，特别是弗雷格和罗素的工作。他开始构思自己的哲学体系，试图解决语言与逻辑的关系问题。这一时期他还与经济学家凯恩斯、诗人艾略特等人建立了友谊，形成了独特的思想圈。1913年，他前往挪威的斯卡弗尤伦独自思考，完成了《逻辑哲学论》的初稿。
points.descriptionEn: In 1911, Wittgenstein traveled to Cambridge University to study logic and philosophy under Bertrand Russell, who quickly recognized his extraordinary talent, calling him 'the most perfect type of genius.' At Cambridge, he delved deeply into logical philosophy, particularly the work of Frege and Russell. He began formulating his own philosophical system, addressing the relationship between language and logic. During this period, he formed friendships with economists Keynes and poets like Eliot. In 1913, he retreated to Skjolden, Norway, to work in solitude, completing the first draft of what would become the 'Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus.'

points.title: 战争经历与《逻辑哲学论》
points.description: 第一次世界大战爆发后，维特根斯坦自愿加入奥地利军队，担任炮兵军官。在前线，他继续哲学思考，随身携带《逻辑哲学论》的手稿。战争经历深刻影响了他，使他更加关注生死问题和伦理价值。1918年，意大利战俘营中，他完成了《逻辑哲学论》的最终版本。这部著作提出了著名的'语言图像论'和'对于不可言说之物必须保持沉默'的观点，认为哲学问题本质上源于语言的误用。战后，他放弃了哲学研究，认为自己已经解决了所有哲学问题，转而当了一名小学教师和园丁。
points.descriptionEn: When World War I broke out, Wittgenstein volunteered for the Austrian army, serving as an artillery officer. At the front, he continued his philosophical work, carrying the manuscript of what would become the 'Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus.' The war profoundly affected him, deepening his contemplation of life, death, and ethical values. In 1918, while held as a prisoner of war in Italy, he completed the final version of the 'Tractatus.' This work introduced his famous 'picture theory of language' and the dictum that 'whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent,' arguing that philosophical problems arise fundamentally from misunderstandings of language. After the war, he abandoned philosophy, believing he had solved all philosophical problems, and became a elementary school teacher and gardener.

points.title: 重返哲学与思想转变
points.titleEn: Return to Philosophy and Intellectual Transformation
points.description: 1929年，维特根斯坦重返剑桥，在罗素的帮助下重新进入学术圈。他最初被视为《逻辑哲学论》的作者，但很快开始质疑自己早期的观点。这一时期，他的思想发生了重大转变，从逻辑原子论转向语言游戏和意义使用理论。他放弃了语言与世界之间的严格对应关系，转而关注语言在不同语境中的实际使用。1939年，他接替G.E.摩尔成为剑桥哲学教授，尽管他对正式教职感到不适。二战期间，他曾在盖伊医院担任实验室助手，后转为圣约翰学院医院的研究工作。这一时期他形成了独特的教学方法，强调哲学对话和具体案例研究，而非抽象理论建构。
points.descriptionEn: In 1929, Wittgenstein returned to Cambridge, with Russell's help re-entering academic circles. Initially regarded as the author of the 'Tractatus,' he soon began to question his earlier views. During this period, he underwent a major intellectual transformation, shifting from logical atomism to theories of language games and meaning as use. He abandoned the strict correspondence between language and world, focusing instead on how language functions in different contexts. In 1939, he succeeded G.E. Moore as Professor of Philosophy at Cambridge, though he was uncomfortable with formal academic duties. During WWII, he worked as a laboratory assistant at Guy's Hospital, later moving to research at St. John's College Hospital. This period saw him develop his distinctive teaching method, emphasizing philosophical dialogue and case studies over abstract theory construction.

points.title: 晚年隐居与哲学反思
points.titleEn: Later Years in Seclusion and Philosophical Reflection
points.description: 1947年，维特根斯坦辞去剑桥教职，前往爱尔兰西海岸的罗斯克里格(Rosscreg)隐居。在生命的最后几年，他继续哲学思考，但不再追求系统的理论建构。这一时期他专注于日常语言哲学和心理学哲学，思考数学基础问题。他的思想更加关注具体生活形式和语言实践，而非抽象理论。尽管健康状况恶化（他患有前列腺癌），他仍坚持工作，直到1951年在剑桥去世。临终前，他告诉朋友'告诉他们我度过了美好的一生'。他的晚期著作《哲学研究》在他去世后出版，标志着他从早期逻辑分析向后期语言哲学的转变，对20世纪哲学产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: In 1947, Wittgenstein resigned his Cambridge post and retreated to Rosscreg on the west coast of Ireland. In his final years, he continued philosophical work but abandoned systematic theory construction. This period focused on ordinary language philosophy and philosophy of psychology, contemplating the foundations of mathematics. His thought became more concerned with concrete forms of life and linguistic practice than abstract theory. Despite deteriorating health (he suffered from prostate cancer), he continued working until his death in Cambridge in 1951. On his deathbed, he told friends 'Tell them I've had a wonderful life.' His posthumously published 'Philosophical Investigations' marked his transformation from early logical analysis to later language philosophy, profoundly influencing 20th-century philosophy.

points.title: 主要著作影响
points.description: 维特根斯坦的主要著作包括1922年出版的《逻辑哲学论》和1953年出版的《哲学研究》。《逻辑哲学论》提出了语言与世界的关系理论，认为命题是现实的图像，哲学问题源于语言的误用，对逻辑实证主义产生了深远影响。而《哲学研究》则代表了他思想的重大转变，提出'语言游戏'概念，强调意义在于使用，而非指称。此外，他的《笔记》、《关于数学基础的评论》等著作在他去世后陆续出版，展现了他思想的发展轨迹。这些作品共同构成了20世纪哲学的重要遗产，影响了分析哲学、语言哲学、心灵哲学等多个领域，也启发了文学、艺术和人文社会科学研究。
points.descriptionEn: Wittgenstein's major works include the 'Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus' (1922) and the 'Philosophical Investigations' (1953). The 'Tractatus' presented his theory of the relationship between language and world, arguing that propositions are pictures of reality and that philosophical problems arise from misunderstandings of language, profoundly influencing logical positivism. The 'Investigations' represented a major shift in his thought, introducing the concept of 'language games' and emphasizing meaning as use rather than reference. Additionally, his 'Notebooks,' 'Remarks on the Foundations of Mathematics,' and other works were published posthumously, revealing the development of his thought. Together, these works constitute a major legacy of 20th-century philosophy, influencing analytic philosophy, philosophy of language, philosophy of mind, and inspiring research in literature, arts, and humanities.

supporter.zh: 维特根斯坦被许多哲学家视为20世纪最伟大的思想家之一。他的贡献在于彻底改变了哲学对语言的理解，将哲学从形而上学的思辨转向对语言实际使用的分析。支持者认为他通过'语言游戏'和'意义即使用'等概念，揭示了传统哲学问题的根源在于语言误用，为哲学研究开辟了新路径。他的思想不仅影响了分析哲学传统，也对文学、艺术、语言学等领域产生了深远影响。维特根斯坦对真理、意义和知识的独特见解，以及对哲学本质的深刻反思，使他成为现代哲学史上不可或缺的人物。
supporter.en: Wittgenstein is regarded by many philosophers as one of the greatest thinkers of the 20th century. His contribution lies in radically transforming philosophy's understanding of language, shifting philosophical inquiry from metaphysical speculation to the analysis of actual language use. Supporters argue that through concepts like 'language games' and 'meaning as use,' he revealed how traditional philosophical problems stem from misunderstandings of language, opening new paths for philosophical inquiry. His thought has influenced not only analytic philosophy but also literature, art, and linguistics. His unique insights on truth, meaning, and knowledge, along with his profound reflections on the nature of philosophy, make him an indispensable figure in modern philosophical history.

critic.zh: 批评者指出维特根斯坦的哲学存在内在矛盾和局限性。首先，他早期和后期思想之间存在明显断裂，使他的哲学体系难以连贯。其次，他对日常语言的过度关注可能导致哲学对科学和形式化思维的忽视。一些批评者认为他的思想过于精英主义，难以应用于实际问题。此外，维特根斯坦对传统哲学的彻底否定有时被视为一种知识上的虚无主义，可能导致哲学失去其探索真理的使命。他的教学方法和个人风格也被批评为专断和不容异见，限制了哲学对话的开放性。
critic.en: Critics point out internal contradictions and limitations in Wittgenstein's philosophy. First, there is a clear rupture between his early and later thought, making his philosophical system difficult to reconcile. Second, his excessive focus on ordinary language may lead philosophy to neglect science and formal thinking. Some critics argue his thought is overly elitist and difficult to apply to practical problems. Additionally, his complete rejection of traditional philosophy is sometimes seen as a form of intellectual nihilism that might deprive philosophy of its mission to seek truth. His teaching methods and personal style have also been criticized as authoritarian and intolerant of dissent, limiting the openness of philosophical dialogue.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，维特根斯坦被定义为一位复杂而矛盾的思想家，既是分析哲学的奠基人之一，又是其最激烈的批判者。他的生平故事——从富家子弟到战时士兵，从小学教师到哲学教授——本身就成为传奇。在流行文化中，他常被描绘为孤独的天才形象，其思想被简化为'不可言说之物必须保持沉默'等格言。学术界则更全面地看待他的贡献，认识到他早期和后期思想的连续性与转变。维特根斯坦的影响超越了哲学领域，渗透到文学、艺术、建筑和心理学等领域，成为现代性反思的重要符号。
objective.en: In historical and popular culture, Wittgenstein is defined as a complex and contradictory thinker—both a founder of analytic philosophy and one of its most fierce critics. His life story—from wealthy heir to wartime soldier, from elementary school teacher to philosophy professor—has become legendary in popular culture, often depicted as a lonely genius whose thought is reduced to maxims like 'whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent.' Academia takes a more comprehensive view of his contributions, recognizing both the continuity and transformation in his early and later thought. Wittgenstein's influence extends beyond philosophy into literature, art, architecture, and psychology, becoming an important symbol of modernity reflection.

self.zh: 语言的界限意味着我的世界的界限。
self.en: The limits of my language mean the limits of my world.

others.zh: 维特根斯坦是唯一一位我认为真正是个天才的哲学家。他的思想深度和原创性无人能及。
others.en: Wittgenstein is the only philosopher I would call a genius. The depth and originality of his thought are unparalleled.
